newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian dealers launch new state debt market.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian dealers launch new state debt market.

text.p: Hungarian securities houses launched a new government debt market on Monday to boost liquidity in government securities trading, Creditanstalt Securities dealer Peter Padanyi told Reuters.
"The new inter-dealer system has begun operation, parallely with the old primary dealer system," Padanyi said.
In the new inter-dealer system, only the 22 primary dealers trade and the obligatory maximum amount is 25 million forints, which is already large enough for the dealers, he added.

Liquidity on the primary dealers' market has been low because dealers are obliged to sell or buy in one deal a maximum of only five million forints of 25 selected government papers at the bid and offer prices they publish, Padanyi said.
Under the new system, each trader also publishes quotes via Reuters screens for only four or five government papers while three brokerages publish quotes for every paper.

In the primary dealer system, introduced in April, 22 primary dealers named by Hungary publish quotes via Reuters screens for six- and 12-month treasury bills and government bonds issued after January 3.
The primary dealer market has only managed to attract a small part of the secondary trading in government securities.

The quote of one company for one government paper in the state-organised primary dealer system and dealers-organised inter-dealer system can be different, Zsolt Wermeser of the Government Debt Management Agency (AAKK) said.
